title: He sees everything, and still He does not rush
subtitle: The Forbearing One who is never provoked and gives time to return
intro: Al-Halim (الْحَلِيمُ) means the Forbearing, the One who sees every act of disobedience, is never provoked into haste, and holds back punishment though He is fully able, giving people time to realise and return. Every day you were not taken for your mistakes was His forbearance.

root.sense: Hilm is composure: a mature, settled mind that is not shaken by provocation or rushed by anger. The same root gives words for reaching maturity and for the intellect. A halim person absorbs harm without exploding; Al-Halim is the perfection of that calm, joined with full power and full knowledge.

row.title: No punishment means no one noticed
He saw, and gave you time

knowing: Al-Halim is the One who is never stirred into haste. He sees disobedience, ingratitude and even insults against Him, and He is not provoked. {idea}He holds back what is deserved, not because He cannot act, but because He chooses to give time.{/idea} The Quran says that if Allah took people to task for what they earn, He would not leave a single creature on the earth, but He defers them to an appointed term (35:45).

The name often comes with Al-Alim, the All-Knowing (22:59, 33:51). That pairing matters. A person can seem patient because he does not know what was done behind his back. {idea}Allah knows everything, and still He is forbearing.{/idea} It also comes with Al-Ghafur (17:44, 35:41): He delays, and then for those who turn back, He forgives.

Human hilm has limits; we hold back until we snap, or we hold back because we are weak. His hilm has neither. It flows from perfect power, perfect knowledge and perfect mercy, and it never turns into indifference. {trap}Mistaking His forbearance for approval is the one way to waste it.{/trap}
seeing: Look at how much room He gives. If you intend a sin and do not do it, it is written for you as a good deed (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim). If you do it, you have your whole life to repent. If you repent, He forgives. Even after death your ongoing charity and the prayers of your children keep reaching you. That is forbearance on forbearance.

At Uhud, a group of believers fled the battle in fear and others paid with their lives. Yet the verse that names their failure declares that Allah has forgiven them, for He is Ghafur and Halim (3:155). He did not forget their years of sacrifice for one moment of fear.

He praised Ibrahim as halim (11:75) when Ibrahim pleaded for more time for the people of Lut. And at Ta'if, bleeding from the stones of the townspeople, the Prophet ﷺ refused the angel's offer to crush them, hoping that their descendants would worship Allah (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim). Millions of believers today come from people who were given time.
trusting: If you are carrying sins you have not yet faced, Al-Halim is the reason you still have a chance. {reward}Each morning you wake up is His forbearance renewed, another day held open for your return.{/reward} Use it before the appointed term arrives.

Trust His hilm also when you watch wrongdoers seem to get away with it. He is not unaware and not unable. He is giving time, and His timing is wiser than your anger. Meanwhile He asks you to carry a share of this name: the Prophet ﷺ told one of his companions that he had two qualities Allah loves, forbearance and deliberateness (Sahih Muslim). {idea}Let the small things go{/idea}, in the shop, in traffic, in your marriage.
loving: Think of all the moments you disobeyed Him in full knowledge that He was watching, and He let the sun rise again, gave you breakfast and kept your heart beating. {reward}A heart that sees this cannot stay hard for long; it softens in shame and then in love.{/reward}
now: Someone cuts you off in traffic and your hand is already on the horn, the words already forming. {idea}Pause for Al-Halim{/idea}. He has seen far worse from you today and has not rushed to answer it. Take your hand off the horn, let the driver go, and keep the calm He has shown you.
old: If Allah has not punished me yet, maybe what I am doing is not that serious.
new: Al-Halim has seen it and is giving me time out of forbearance; this delay is an invitation to return.
try: The next time something small irritates you today, deliberately let it pass without comment, for the sake of Al-Halim.

dua.text: Ya Halim, You have seen my faults and still given me time. Do not take me before I return to You, and give me a share of Your forbearance with those who hurt me.
dua.note: Call on Him as Al-Halim when you fear you have pushed too far; His holding back is the space in which repentance happens.

pairs.why: Alim Halim: He knows everything that is done, and still He is forbearing.
Shakur Halim: He multiplies the little good we give and bears patiently with our shortfalls (64:17).
Al-Halim is calm that is never provoked; As-Sabur is endurance that holds a matter back until its appointed time.

faq.a: Al-Halim means the Forbearing. He sees disobedience and is never provoked into haste; He holds back punishment though He is fully able, giving people time to repent. The root h-l-m refers to a calm, mature mind that is not shaken by anger.

faq.q: What is the difference between Al-Halim and As-Sabur?
faq.a: Both describe Allah not hastening punishment. Al-Halim emphasises composure: He is not stirred by provocation and often pardons. As-Sabur emphasises endurance over time: He bears what His creatures say and do and defers the matter to an appointed time.

faq.q: Why does Al-Halim appear with Al-Alim and Al-Ghafur?
faq.a: With Al-Alim, it shows His forbearance is not ignorance; He knows everything and still holds back. With Al-Ghafur, it shows where His delay leads for those who use it well: He gives time, and when they return, He forgives (17:44, 35:41).
